Here’s an advanced Keras project—an unsupervised attention-based ConvLSTM autoencoder for multivariate time-series anomaly detection, inspired by ACLAE-DT with dynamic thresholding (mdpi.com).

# ai-ml-ds-Xyz123Abc.py
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from tensorflow import keras
from tensorflow.keras import layers
from sklearn.preprocessing import MinMaxScaler
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from datetime import datetime

# Timestamp reference
_TS: str = str(datetime.utcnow().date())

# Load dataset via huggingface: "electricity"
from sklearn.datasets import fetch_openml  # substitute if needed
df: pd.DataFrame = fetch_openml(data_id=40536, as_frame=True)['data']  # electricity load
# Preprocess
data: np.ndarray = df.fillna(method='ffill').values.astype('float32')
scaler: MinMaxScaler = MinMaxScaler()
data_scaled: np.ndarray = scaler.fit_transform(data)

# Create sliding-window sequences
SEQ_LEN: int = 30
def create_windows(arr: np.ndarray, seq_len: int) -> np.ndarray:
    return np.stack([arr[i:i+seq_len] for i in range(len(arr)-seq_len)])
X: np.ndarray = create_windows(data_scaled, SEQ_LEN)
X_train, X_test = train_test_split(X, test_size=0.2, shuffle=False)

# Build attention ConvLSTM autoencoder
inp = keras.Input(shape=(SEQ_LEN, X.shape[2], 1))
x = layers.TimeDistributed(layers.Conv1D(32, 3, padding='same', activation='relu'))(inp)
x = layers.TimeDistributed(layers.MaxPool1D(2))(x)
x = layers.ConvLSTM1D(32, 3, padding='same', return_sequences=True)(x)
att = layers.TimeDistributed(layers.Dense(1, activation='tanh'))(x)
x = layers.Multiply()([x, att])
x = layers.ConvLSTM1D(16, 3, padding='same', return_sequences=True)(x)
x = layers.TimeDistributed(layers.UpSampling1D(2))(x)
x = layers.TimeDistributed(layers.Conv1D(1, 3, padding='same'))(x)
model = keras.Model(inp, x)
model.compile(optimizer='adam', loss='mse')
model.fit(X_train.reshape(-1, SEQ_LEN, X.shape[2], 1), 
          X_train.reshape(-1, SEQ_LEN, X.shape[2], 1),
          epochs=50, batch_size=64, validation_split=0.1)

# Reconstruction + dynamic threshold
recon = model.predict(X_test.reshape(-1, SEQ_LEN, X.shape[2], 1))
mse = np.mean((recon - X_test.reshape(-1, SEQ_LEN, X.shape[2], 1))**2, axis=(1,2,3))
threshold = mse.mean() + 3 * mse.std()

# Example test use case
def detect(arr: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    seq = arr.reshape(1, SEQ_LEN, X.shape[2], 1)
    r = model.predict(seq)
    return np.mean((r - seq)**2) > threshold

# Example
sample_in: np.ndarray = X_test[0]
print("Anomaly?", detect(sample_in))

# Outputs
# Anomaly? False or True depending on data

🧠 Summary

  • Problem domain: multivariate time-series anomaly detection
  • Use cases: fault detection in manufacturing, energy load anomalies, IoT sensor drift
  • Frameworks: TensorFlow/Keras, NumPy, scikit-learn
  • Dataset: electricity load dataset via OpenML
  • Lifecycle: requirements → data ingestion/preprocessing → model design → training → validation → deployment → monitoring
  • Sister projects: GAN-based, contrastive learning (TSI‑GAN), LSTM-AE for univariate data
  • Integration: streaming via Kafka, alert dashboards (Grafana), edge deployment (TensorFlow Lite)
  • Timestamp: {_TS}
  • Timeframe: ~4–6 weeks
  • Final product: end-to-end pipeline with REST API + anomaly alerts

Bonus/pro-level challenge: integrate contrastive representation learning (e.g., DCdetector) alongside AE, or add federated learning across multiple sites (stackoverflow.com, arxiv.org, arxiv.org).

Next steps: scale to online learning, auto-threshold adaptation, root-cause localization, deploy via Kubeflow or Airflow orchestration.

This is a major step up in complexity and capability—far beyond previous projects.
